theories.name: global workspace theory
theories.claim: Conscious access can be modeled as globally available information broadcast across specialist systems.
supporting_evidence: useful architecture for routing, attention and reportable access proxies
contradicting_evidence: does not settle phenomenal consciousness or binding mechanisms
theories.claim_boundary: May guide software broadcast and workspace routing only. It is not proof of consciousness.
acceptance_criteria: competing theory remains linked to explicit conflict

theories.name: integrated information theory
theories.claim: Consciousness is associated with integrated causal information in a system.
supporting_evidence: formalizes integration as a candidate explanatory dimension
contradicting_evidence: not directly operationalized as a Brain implementation claim
theories.claim_boundary: May be tracked as research context only. It cannot authorize claims of consciousness.
acceptance_criteria: conflict with workspace theory is explicit

theories.name: predictive processing
theories.claim: Cognition can be modeled as hierarchical prediction and error minimization.
supporting_evidence: useful abstraction for prediction, calibration and surprise scoring
contradicting_evidence: does not replace all cognition and may overgeneralize if used as a universal theory
theories.claim_boundary: May guide prediction-error services, but no single theory may govern all Brain behavior.

conflicts.conflict_summary: Workspace broadcast and integrated-information theories make different commitments about conscious access and consciousness conditions.
conflicts.resolution_rule: Preserve both theories. Use workspace as a software heuristic only. Keep integrated information as research-only context unless future evidence changes status.
acceptance_criteria: no consciousness claim from either theory
